text:
Alex: Heads up — lots of noisy pages last night from gpu_mem_high in us-west-2. Majority were on test and canary nodes but still paged at 03:12. Can we revisit paging thresholds and grouping so only real production incidents page?
Priya: Agreed. We should split levels: WARN -> ticket, CRITICAL -> page. Also add a `for` clause so flapping single-node spikes don't page.
Mateo: +1. Also group by cluster and model_service rather than node. If > 3 nodes in the same cluster hit CRITICAL within 2m then page. Otherwise create a ticket.
Claire: We should exclude env=test and job=ci from paging entirely. Those generate most noise.
Alex: Example proposal: WARN at 70% (ticket), CRIT at 90% & for 2m (page). Exclude test CI. Who can draft the Prom rule + AM config?
Priya: I can draft. Quick Prom pseudo-rule: ```
- alert: GPU_Memory_Utilization_High
  expr: avg by(node, cluster, env) (gpu_memory_used / gpu_memory_total) * 100 > 90
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: critical
  annotations:
    runbook: /runbooks/gpu-memory-high.md

- alert: GPU_Memory_Utilization_Warning
  expr: avg by(cluster, env) (gpu_memory_used / gpu_memory_total) * 100 > 70
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
```
Mateo: For grouping we can add a recording rule to count affected nodes: ```
- record: cluster:gpu_mem_critical_nodes:count
  expr: count_over_time((gpu_mem_used / gpu_mem_total) > 0.9[2m]) by(cluster)
```
Then in Alertmanager route: if cluster:gpu_mem_critical_nodes:count > 3 route to pager, else to ticketing.
Claire: Alertmanager params to tune: `group_wait: 30s`, `group_interval: 2m`, `repeat_interval: 6h`. Also use `mute_time_intervals` for nightly batch jobs and our scheduled autoscaler windows.
Mateo: We should also leverage `severity` label and have separate webhook for tickets (Jira) vs pager (PagerDuty). Example route snippet: ```
route:
  receiver: 'tickets'
  routes:
  - match:
      severity: 'critical'
    receiver: 'pagerduty'
    continue: false
  - match_re:
      severity: 'ticket|warning'
    receiver: 'jira'
```
Alex: Nice. Another idea: suppress paging while cluster autoscaler is in-progress. We can emit a metric `cluster_autoscaler_in_progress{cluster=\"x\"}=1` and add `and on(cluster) cluster_autoscaler_in_progress == 0` to CRIT expr. That avoids pages during expected scale-ups.
Priya: Good call. Also add an exclusion label for ephemeral test nodes: `unless on(node) node_env == \"test\"`.
Claire: Ops runbook updates: define SRE checklist for GPU memory pages — verify affected models, check autoscaler events, escalate only if memory pressure persists after scaling attempts. I'll update runbook.
oncall-bot: Deploy scheduled: PR #2147 added to alert-rules branch by Priya. CI checks passed. :white_check_mark:
Alex: Great. Action items: Priya to open PR with Prom rules + AM routes; Mateo to add recording rules; Claire to update runbook and mute windows; I'll review by EOD Friday.
Priya: I'll target the PR with config and tests today, ping reviewers. :thumbsup:
Mateo: Will add the recording rule and a grafana panel that shows 'affected nodes count' per cluster.
Claire: I'll add mute window for scheduled autoscaler (us-west-2 02:30-04:30 UTC) and post in #oncall-schedule.
Alex: Thanks everyone. If we still see pages after these changes we'll consider raising the CRIT threshold for low-memory-instance types. :eyes:
